title: Semantic Communication on Digital Wireless Communication System
content: Semantic communication has become a hot research topic in recent years. However, it faces an urgent and crucial issue that how semantic communication can be compatible with current wireless systems. To address this issue, we propose a bit-conversion-based transmission framework to make the balance between the modifications of the existing wireless systems and the advantages of semantic communication. Specifically, a specific physical layer procedure including binary conversion coding, rate matching, packet tail detection, and demodulation hard decision is designed to make the end-to-end (E2E) transmission work. Furthermore, a semantic communication simulator is developed to implement this framework. In order to optimize the performance of this framework, a novel physical layer metric, integer error rate (IER), is proposed as a physical layer metric for semantic information transmission. We also prove that IER is more suitable than bit error rate (BER) for the evaluation of semantic communication by simulations. On the basis of IER, a minimum Manhattan distance constellation mapping scheme is proposed, which can improve the transmission quality of semantic communication under the same BER condition. To release the limitation of this constellation mapping scheme that the semantic quantization output has to be bound with the modulation order, we proposed a hybrid JSCC/SSCC transmission scheme, which can separate the semantic quantization output from the modulation order by segmenting the bits to be transmitted. At the same time, the simulation results verified that the hybrid JSCC/SSCC transmission scheme can improve the transmission quality of semantic communication at the low SNR range while saving the bandwidth 50% compared to the benchmark schemes.
